source.title: Development of Optically-Controlled “Living Electrodes” with Long-Projecting Axon Tracts for a Synaptic Brain-Machine Interface

material: µTENN (micro-tissue engineered neural network) living electrode in microcolumn

culture_days.evidence: Video 2 shows a bidirectional µTENN approximately 1.1mm in length, imaged at 10 days in vitro.

other_outcomes.value: GCaMP-positive µTENN neurons and processes within and immediately surrounding the construct
other_outcomes.evidence: Multiphoton image of the µTENN from (A) at one-month post-implant, showing GCaMP-positive µTENN neurons and processes within and immediately surrounding the construct.
other_outcomes.name: persistence of GCaMP-positive neurons in vivo

other_outcomes.value: synapsin+ puncta at and around the µTENN/brain interface
other_outcomes.evidence: Confocal image of a µTENN at one-month post implant, with synapsin+ puncta at and around the µTENN/brain interface.
other_outcomes.name: synaptic integration

other_outcomes.evidence: Single frames from multiphoton recording of the µTENN from (a-b) at 10 days post-implant during low activity (left), breathing (middle), and non-artifact neuronal activity (right).
other_outcomes.name: in vivo calcium activity

notes: Part 2 contains only figure/video captions; implanted under cranial window with PDMS rings and glass coverslip. Optical stimulation at 470 nm, 106-634 mW/mm2 at 10 DIV.
